docs.title: Welcome To Ossum Inc.'s Technology!
docs.text:
This site provides documentation for technologies created at Ossum, Inc.

The sections at the top correspond to Ossum Inc's main products:

  • RIDDL - The specification language behind everything else, and its compiler riddlc
  • riddlg - The generator: turns a validated RIDDL model into documentation, API specifications, schemas, catalogs and code
  • Synapify - The workbench for RIDDL models, with visual editing, simulation and generation
  • IDE help - Open source editor support: the IntelliJ plugin and the VS Code extension

docs.title: About Ossum Inc.
docs.text: Ossum Inc. builds tools that make designing distributed systems accessible to domain experts—not just seasoned architects.

docs.title: Our Mission
docs.text:
Complex software systems are hard to build. The gap between what business experts understand and what developers implement is where projects fail. Requirements get lost in translation, designs drift from intent, and systems end up solving yesterday's problems.

We believe there's a better way.

RIDDL (Reactive Interface to Domain Definition Language) bridges this gap by providing a specification language that domain experts can read and contribute to, while being precise enough for AI-assisted code generation. It's Domain-Driven Design made practical.

docs.title: The Story
docs.text:
RIDDL began in 2019, born from decades of experience building large-scale distributed systems. After watching project after project struggle with the same problems—miscommunication between business and technical teams, designs that couldn't keep up with changing requirements, implementations that drifted from specifications—founder Reid Spencer started asking: What if the specification itself was the source of truth?

The first commits landed in late 2021. Reactific Software LLC, the original home of RIDDL, was acquired by Ossum Inc. in 2022 to continue the vision: making distributed system design accessible to everyone who understands the domain, not just those who can write code.

docs.title: Search all documentation
docs.text:
There are two search fields, and they cover different things.

Field Searches The box in the title bar only the site and version you are reading Full Search, just below it every product at once

The reason for two is that the documentation is published as several independent sites — one per product, each with its own versions — and each site builds its own search index. That per-site index is what makes the title-bar box precise: on the RIDDL 1.31 pages it returns 1.31 answers, not answers from a release you are not reading.

Full Search is built separately, over the published pages of every product, so it can find things the title-bar box cannot — searching for "Synapify" from inside the RIDDL documentation, for instance.

It covers the current release of each product, plus the pages on this site. Older releases are deliberately left out: each product publishes several versions and every alias is a full copy, so including them would return the same page three or four times. To search within an older release, open it and use the title-bar box.

Search index unavailable

The full-site search index could not be loaded. It is rebuilt after the documentation is published, so it may be briefly missing after a release. The title-bar box is unaffected.

docs.title: IDE Support for RIDDL
docs.text: Ossum Inc. provides IDE extensions for working with the RIDDL language. All tools are free and open source under the Apache License 2.0.

docs.title: IntelliJ IDEA Plugin
docs.text:
RIDDL language support for JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA, including:

  • Syntax highlighting with customizable colors
  • Real-time validation and error detection
  • Integrated RIDDL tool window
  • Clickable error navigation

Status: Beta - Download

docs.title: VS Code Extension
docs.text:
RIDDL language support for Visual Studio Code, including:

  • Syntax highlighting with semantic tokens
  • IntelliSense code completion (50+ keywords)
  • Real-time diagnostics
  • Go to Definition and Find References
  • Hover documentation

Status: Beta - Download

docs.title: Authoring RIDDL Sources
docs.text:
A comprehensive guide to writing effective RIDDL source files, covering:

  • File organization and includes
  • Adding metadata with the with clause
  • Type definitions and references
  • Commands, events, queries, and results
  • Entity design patterns
  • Handler statements
  • Common patterns and best practices

This guide applies to any IDE or editor.

docs.title: RIDDL MCP Server
docs.text:
Connect AI assistants to the RIDDL MCP Server for intelligent modeling assistance:

  • Validate RIDDL code with detailed error messages
  • Check model completeness and get suggestions
  • Convert natural language to RIDDL structures
  • Get explanations for validation errors

Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, VS Code Copilot, IntelliJ AI Assistant, and IntelliJ Junie.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Install an IDE extension for your preferred editor
  2. Read the authoring guide to learn RIDDL best practices
  3. Connect the MCP server for AI-assisted modeling (optional)

docs.title: IntelliJ IDEA Plugin for RIDDL
docs.text:
The RIDDL4IDEA plugin provides comprehensive support for the RIDDL language in IntelliJ IDEA, including syntax highlighting, real-time validation, and integrated error navigation.

Release Notes

docs.title: Beta Program
docs.text:
The plugin is currently in beta.

To install:

  1. Download the latest .zip release from the GitHub Release Assets page
  2. In IntelliJ IDEA, go to Settings > Plugins
  3. Click the gear icon and select Install Plugin from Disk...
  4. Select the downloaded .zip file
  5. Restart IntelliJ IDEA

docs.title: Marketplace (Coming Soon)
docs.text:
When version 1.0 is released, the plugin will be available from the JetBrains Marketplace:

  1. Go to Settings > Plugins > Marketplace
  2. Search for "RIDDL"
  3. Click Install

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or later (Community or Ultimate Edition)
  • JDK 25 or later

docs.title: Syntax Highlighting
docs.text:
The plugin provides rich syntax highlighting for RIDDL files:

Element Color (Dark Theme) Keywords Purple (#c77dbb) Punctuation Teal (#0da19e) Readability words Yellow (#b3ae60) Identifiers Default text Comments Gray Strings Green Numbers Blue

docs.title: Customizing Colors
docs.text:
To customize the RIDDL color scheme:

  1. Go to Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > RIDDL
  2. Adjust colors for each token type
  3. Click Apply

The plugin includes a dark theme based on Darcula. Light themes use IDE defaults but are fully customizable.

docs.title: Real-Time Validation
docs.text:
As you type, the plugin validates your RIDDL source and displays errors inline:

  • Syntax errors appear immediately as you type
  • Semantic errors (undefined references, type mismatches) show after parsing
  • Errors appear as squiggly underlines in the editor
  • Click errors in the console to jump to the source location

docs.title: RIDDL Tool Window
docs.text: The plugin adds a RIDDL tool window to the left sidebar with:

docs.title: Toolbar Actions
docs.text: Action Icon Description New Window + Create additional analysis tabs Compile Build Run RIDDL validation Settings Gear Open project configuration

docs.title: Console Output
docs.text:
The console displays:

  • Validation results with severity (Error, Warning, Info)
  • File locations with line and column numbers
  • Clickable links to navigate directly to problems

docs.title: Multiple Tabs
docs.text:
Create multiple tabs to work with different RIDDL configurations:

  1. Click the + button to create a new tab
  2. Configure each tab with different settings
  3. Right-click a tab to rename it
  4. Close tabs you no longer need (first tab cannot be closed)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Access settings via Settings > Tools > RIDDL Project Settings or click the gear icon in the RIDDL tool window.

docs.title: Path Configuration
docs.text: Setting Description Top-level .riddl file Your project's main RIDDL file (entry point for validation) Configuration file Optional .conf file for advanced commands

docs.title: Validation Command
docs.text:
Choose which RIDDL command to run:

Command Purpose about Display RIDDL version information info Show system information from Load configuration from file (requires config file)

docs.title: Validation Options
docs.text: Fine-tune validation behavior with these options:

docs.title: Message Display
docs.text: Option Description Show warnings Display warning messages Show missing warnings Warn about undefined references Show style warnings Warn about style violations Show usage warnings Warn about unused definitions Show info messages Display informational messages

docs.title: Output Control
docs.text: Option Description Verbose Enable detailed output Quiet Suppress normal output Debug Enable debug information Show times Display parsing duration

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Option Description Warnings are fatal Treat warnings as errors Sort by location Group messages by file location

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Option Range Description Max parallel parsing 1 - 2x CPUs Threads for parallel file parsing Max include wait < 60000 ms Timeout for include file processing

docs.title: Auto-Parse on Save
docs.text: When enabled (default), the plugin automatically re-validates your RIDDL files whenever you save. Disable this for large projects where validation takes significant time.

docs.title: Tool Window Actions
docs.text: The RIDDL tool window provides these actions:

docs.title: Compile/Validate
docs.text:
Click the Build icon or use the keyboard:

  • Parses your top-level RIDDL file
  • Validates all included files
  • Displays results in the console
  • Updates editor annotations

docs.title: Navigate to Error
docs.text:
Click any error message in the console to:

  1. Open the containing file (if not already open)
  2. Jump to the exact line and column
  3. Position cursor at the error location

docs.title: Clear Output
docs.text: Right-click in the console and select Clear to reset the output.

docs.title: File Types
docs.text:
The plugin recognizes files with the .riddl extension:

  • Automatic syntax highlighting when opened
  • Icon displayed in project tree
  • Full validation support

docs.title: Setting Up a New Project
docs.text:
1. Create your main .riddl file (e.g., myproject.riddl)
  2. Open RIDDL Project Settings
  3. Set the Top-level .riddl file to your main file
  4. Enable desired validation options
  5. Click Compile to validate

docs.title: Working with Include Files
docs.text:
The plugin follows all include directives from your top-level file:

// myproject.riddl
domain MyProject is {
  include "contexts/orders.riddl"
  include "types/common.riddl"
}

All included files are validated together, ensuring cross-file references resolve correctly.

docs.title: Understanding Validation Messages
docs.text:
Messages include severity and location:

Error: [orders.riddl:42:15] Undefined reference to type 'CustomerID'
Warning: [types.riddl:10:1] Missing brief description for type 'Address'

Click the message to navigate to orders.riddl, line 42, column 15.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
For large projects:

  • Disable Auto-parse on save and validate manually
  • Increase Max parallel parsing on multi-core systems
  • Use separate tool window tabs for different subsystems

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
The plugin does not register global keyboard shortcuts. All actions are accessible through:

  • The RIDDL tool window toolbar
  • Right-click context menus
  • Settings dialogs

Standard IntelliJ shortcuts work in RIDDL files:

Shortcut Action Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) Save (triggers auto-validation if enabled) Ctrl+Shift+F Reformat code Ctrl+/ Toggle line comment Ctrl+Shift+/ Toggle block comment

docs.title: Plugin Not Loading
docs.text:
• Verify IntelliJ IDEA version is 2024.1 or later
  • Check Settings > Plugins > Installed for RIDDL4IDEA
  • Try disabling and re-enabling the plugin

docs.title: No Syntax Highlighting
docs.text:
• Verify file has .riddl extension
  • Check Settings > Editor > File Types for RIDDL registration
  • Restart IntelliJ IDEA

docs.title: Validation Not Running
docs.text:
• Ensure Top-level .riddl file is configured in settings
  • Check the file path is correct and file exists
  • Look for error messages in the RIDDL console

docs.title: Slow Validation
docs.text:
• Reduce Max parallel parsing if memory is limited
  • Disable Show style warnings and Show usage warnings for faster runs
  • Consider splitting large models into smaller include files

docs.title: VS Code Extension for RIDDL
docs.text:
The RIDDL Language Support extension provides comprehensive development tools for the RIDDL language in Visual Studio Code, including intelligent code completion, real-time diagnostics, and code navigation.

Release Notes

docs.title: Beta Program
docs.text:
The extension is currently in beta. To install:

  1. Download the .vsix file from GitHub Release Assets
  2. Open VS Code
  3. Press Cmd+Shift+P (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows/Linux)
  4. Type "Install from VSIX" and select it
  5. Browse to the downloaded .vsix file
  6. Click Install and reload VS Code

Or via command line:

code --install-extension /path/to/riddl-vscode-0.9.0-beta.vsix

docs.title: VS Code Marketplace (Coming Soon)
docs.text:
When version 1.0 is released, installation will be simpler:

  1. Open VS Code
  2. Click the Extensions tab in the left sidebar
  3. Search for "RIDDL"
  4. Click Install

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• VS Code 1.75.0 or later
  • No additional runtime dependencies (RIDDL parser is bundled)

docs.title: Syntax Highlighting
docs.text:
The extension provides rich syntax highlighting using both TextMate grammar (fast initial highlighting) and semantic tokens (context-aware refinement):

Element Description Keywords domain, context, entity, type, command, event, etc. Predefined Types String, Integer, Boolean, Timestamp, UUID, etc. Readability Words is, of, by, for, to, from, with, and, etc. Comments Line (//) and block (/* */) comments Strings Quoted string literals with escape sequences Documentation Markdown lines starting with \|

docs.title: Code Completion (IntelliSense)
docs.text: Press Ctrl+Space to trigger completion, or just start typing. The extension provides:

docs.title: Keywords with Snippets
docs.text:
Over 50 keywords with intelligent snippets:

Keyword Snippet Produces domain Full domain structure with braces context Context definition template entity Entity with state and handlers type Type definition command Command message definition event Event message definition handler Handler with on clause template saga Saga with steps template

Example: Type entity and press Tab:

entity Name is {
  // cursor here
}

docs.title: Predefined Types
docs.text:
All RIDDL predefined types with documentation:

  • String, Integer, Number, Boolean, Decimal
  • Date, Time, DateTime, Timestamp, Duration
  • Id, UUID, URL, UserId
  • List, Set, Map, Sequence
  • And more...

docs.title: Readability Words
docs.text:
Structural keywords that improve RIDDL readability:

  • is, of, by, for, to, from, with
  • and, or, not, in, on, at

docs.title: Hover Documentation
docs.text:
Hover over any keyword, type, or readability word to see documentation:

  • Keywords: Comprehensive descriptions with usage notes
  • Types: Type-specific documentation with examples
  • Readability Words: Explanations of structural role
  • User Definitions: Location information (line/column)

docs.title: Real-Time Diagnostics
docs.text:
The extension validates your RIDDL as you type:

Severity Indicator Examples Error Red squiggly Syntax errors, undefined references Warning Yellow squiggly Missing documentation, style issues Info Blue squiggly Suggestions and hints

Diagnostics integrate with the VS Code Problems panel (Cmd+Shift+M).

Performance

Validation is debounced by 500ms to avoid excessive parsing while typing.

docs.title: Go to Definition
docs.text:
Navigate to where a symbol is defined:

  • Press F12 with cursor on a symbol
  • Or Cmd + click (Mac) / Ctrl + click (Windows/Linux)

Works for:

  • Type definitions
  • Entity, context, domain references
  • Command, event, query references

docs.title: Find All References
docs.text:
Find everywhere a symbol is used:

  • Press Shift+F12 with cursor on a symbol
  • Or right-click and select Find All References

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Access commands via the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P):

docs.title: RIDDL: Version Information
docs.text:
Shows RIDDL build information including:

  • RIDDL library version
  • Build date
  • Scala/sbt versions
  • Feature list
  • Documentation links

docs.title: RIDDL: Parse Current File
docs.text:
Parses the active .riddl file and displays:

  • Full AST structure (JSON format)
  • Parse errors with locations

Useful for debugging complex syntax issues.

docs.title: RIDDL: Validate Current File
docs.text:
Runs full validation (syntax + semantic) and shows:

  • Error count
  • Warning count
  • Info message count
  • Detailed messages with locations

docs.title: RIDDL: Translate to Output Format
docs.text: Placeholder for future translation features. Shows available riddlc commands.

docs.title: Extension Commands
docs.text: Shortcut Command Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P Open Command Palette (type "RIDDL" to filter)

docs.title: Code Navigation
docs.text: Shortcut Action F12 Go to Definition Shift+F12 Find All References Cmd + click / Ctrl + click Go to Definition Ctrl+Space Trigger code completion

docs.title: Editor Features
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+/ / Ctrl+/ Toggle line comment (//) Shift+Alt+A Toggle block comment (/* */) Cmd+Shift+[ / Ctrl+Shift+[ Fold region Cmd+Shift+] / Ctrl+Shift+] Unfold region

docs.title: Built-in RIDDL Editor Features
docs.text:
The extension configures these editor behaviors:

  • Auto-closing brackets: {, [, (, ", and triple backticks
  • Bracket matching: All bracket types highlighted
  • Code folding: Fold on braces and //region markers
  • Smart indentation: Automatic indent after opening brackets

docs.title: Output Panel
docs.text:
Commands write results to the RIDDL output channel:

  1. Open View > Output (or Cmd+Shift+U)
  2. Select RIDDL from the dropdown

Output includes:

  • Command results with formatting
  • Numbered error/warning messages
  • Clean text (ANSI codes stripped)

docs.title: File Association
docs.text:
The extension automatically activates for files with the .riddl extension:

  • Language ID: riddl
  • File Icon: Custom RIDDL icon (light and dark variants)
  • Content Type: Text with RIDDL grammar

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The extension works out-of-the-box with sensible defaults. No user configuration is required.

docs.title: Editor Settings for RIDDL
docs.text:
You can customize VS Code editor settings specifically for RIDDL files:

{
  "[riddl]": {
    "editor.tabSize": 2,
    "editor.insertSpaces": true,
    "editor.formatOnSave": false,
    "editor.wordWrap": "on"
  }
}

docs.title: Semantic Highlighting
docs.text:
Semantic highlighting is enabled by default. To disable:

{
  "editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled": false
}

docs.title: Efficient Editing
docs.text:
1. Use snippets: Type a keyword and press Tab for full structure
  2. Hover for docs: Check documentation without leaving the editor
  3. Navigate quickly: F12 to jump to definitions, Alt+Left to go back
  4. Check Problems panel: Cmd+Shift+M for all issues at a glance

docs.title: Working with Large Models
docs.text:
1. Use folding: Collapse sections you're not editing
  2. Split editor: Work on multiple files side-by-side
  3. Use includes: Break large models into smaller files
// main.riddl
domain MyProject is {
  include "contexts/orders.riddl"
  include "contexts/inventory.riddl"
}

docs.title: Understanding Errors
docs.text:
Error messages include file location:

[orders.riddl:42:15] Error: Undefined reference to type 'CustomerID'

This means: orders.riddl, line 42, column 15.

Click the error in the Problems panel to jump directly to the location.

docs.title: Validation Source Labels
docs.text:
Diagnostics show their source:

  • RIDDL - Parse/syntax errors
  • RIDDL (validation) - Semantic validation errors/warnings
  • RIDDL (info) - Informational messages

docs.title: Extension Not Activating
docs.text:
• Verify file has .riddl extension
  • Check Output > Extension Host for errors
  • Try Developer: Reload Window

docs.title: No Syntax Highlighting
docs.text:
• Check file type in status bar (should show "RIDDL")
  • Verify extension is enabled in Extensions panel
  • Try disabling other extensions that might conflict

docs.title: Slow Performance
docs.text:
• Large files may take longer to parse
  • Semantic highlighting has 500ms debounce
  • Check for syntax errors that might confuse the parser

docs.title: Errors Not Showing
docs.text:
• Check Problems panel is visible (Cmd+Shift+M)
  • Verify the file has been saved (diagnostics run on save)
  • Look for parse errors that might prevent full validation
